name: Distribución de Palabras Funcionales
description: Analiza the distribución of palabras funcionales (articles, prepositions, conjunctions) as stylistic fingerprints to distinguish AI from texto humano.
useCase: Detecting AI text through abnormal function word usage patrones that reflect unconscious estilo de escritura
mechanism: Extrae and quantifies palabras funcionales (determiners, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliary verbs, pronombres) que constitute ~50% of typical English text. These 'style words' are produced largely unconsciously by humans and carry strong authorial fingerprints. The method computes relative frequencies of 300+ palabras funcionales and compares distribucións using Burrows's Delta distance metric. generado por IA text shows estadísticoly distinct function word profiles from texto humano.
source: Burrows, J. F. (2002) - Delta: A Measure of Stylistic Difference, Literary and Linguistic Computing
algorithm: Function Word Extraction + Burrows's Delta + Kilgarriff's Chi-Squared
parameters: Function word list: 300+ closed-class words, Metric: Burrows's Delta, z-score normalization, Granularity: per-paragraph, Reference: balanced human corpus
strengths:
• Grounded in decades of computational stylistics research
• Function words are difficult to consciously control
• Robust a través de topics and domains
• Well-understood estadístico framework
limitations:
• Requires sufficient text length (>200 words)
• May not distinguish entre different human authors vs AI
• Language-specific function word lists needed
• Modern LLMs increasingly match human distribucións

references.title: Burrows, J. F. (2002). Delta: A Measure of Stylistic Difference and Its Literary History. Literary and Linguistic Computing.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Kestemont, M. (2014). Function Words in Authorship Attribution: From Black Magic to Theory? EACL Workshop.
